OGS, Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e Geofisica Sperimentale (National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics) is an internationally oriented public research institution. This institution operates and develops its own mission in the European Research Area (ERA) and internationally, prioritizing the basic and applied research fields of:

Oceanography (under the Physical, Chemical and Biological aspects);
Geophysics and Marine Geology;
Experimental and Explorative Geophysics.

entityDescription: The Studium Generalis Kalaritanum was founded in 1620 along the lines of the old Spanish Universities of Salamanca, Valladolid and Lérida. It originally offered Law, Latin, Greek and Hebrew Literature, the Liberal Arts, Medicine, Surgery, Philosophy and Science. When Sardinia passed under the House of Savoy government in the 18th century, the statute of the University was significantly modified, with the expansion of the science faculties and institutes. Designed by the Piedmontese engineer Saverio Belgrano di Famolasco, the new University building was completed at the end of the 18th century. Today it hosts the Rectorate and the administrative offices. The 19th and 20th centuries saw more and more emphasis placed on research activities, with the achievement of important, internationally acclaimed results, especially in the fields of Medicine, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Archaeology. In the 20th century, problems arising from severe damage to University buildings during the Second World War had to be addressed, and reconstruction is only now approaching its final phase. At the end of the 1960s ambitious plans were advanced for residential university structures in a campus style.

entityName: FONDAZIONE ISI - ISTITUTO PER L'INTERSCAMBIO SCIENTIFICO
entityDescription: The ISI foundation has been established in 1988 in Torino, where it still has its headquarter. In 2014 ISI established together with the Fondazione Sviluppo e Crescita CRT the related sister ISI Global Science Foundation in New York. The history of ISI is long and exciting, marked and characterized by a number of crucial steps and visionary men behind them: to begin with, intellectuals such as Carl Kaysen, Thomas Kuhn and Salva Luria, under the guide of the first President, Tullio Regge and later Mario Rasetti. Since its very beginning, ISI promoted a distinctive borderless attitude, which allowed it to draw an endless arc through time, space, disciplines and research domain to fulfill its continued commitment to its values. By proactively meeting these scientific challenges, ISI has nurtured the creation of a distributed network of top-notch researchers which enables a valuable knowledge exchange with targeted stakeholders, such as the broader scientific community, philanthropists, global foundations, governments and corporations in order to contribute to social, economic and cultural growth at global scale. Within the overarching domain of Complexity Science, the ISI Foundation leverages the competing contributions of Data and Theory to avoid the silos of science too prevalent elsewhere. The combination of data, theory and impact is the founding essence of all the ISI research domains, which feed each other through borderless collaborations among multidisciplinary scientists, providing a solid, growing and high-potential knowledge capital that can be leveraged in all possible endeavors. The exciting Scientific story of ISI was a long difficult but beautiful path whose horizon is as unpredictable and challenging, but stimulating and exciting as the exploration of the very frontiers of new science can be.

The combination of data, theory and impact is the founding essence of all the ISI research domains, which feed each other through borderless collaborations among multidisciplinary scientists, providing a solid, growing and high-potential knowledge capital that can be leveraged in all possible endeavors. The exciting Scientific story of ISI was a long difficult but beautiful path whose horizon is as unpredictable and challenging, but stimulating and exciting as the exploration of the very frontiers of new science can be.

entityDescription:
Vianet is an Italian SME founded in 1993. It uses technologies to transform organizations and their processes, enabling them to be competitive, innovate their services, and improve performance while reducing costs.
Its competence includes international pilot projects with KPI definition, measurement, and verification involving citizens, stakeholders, and final users.
Its staff has participated in 500+ projects, sometimes as work package leaders and participating in project management.
Activities
- Definition and development of solutions using the most suitable technologies and methodologies (participatory design, Agile) to demonstrate, measure, and evaluate them in pilot cases and living labs
- Improvement of the customer experience and citizens, stakeholders, and tourists’ involvement in territories, communities, archaeological and cultural sites
- Communication, dissemination, and exploitation.
 
Vianet has been an ordinary member and center of excellence of DTC (District of Cultural Technologies) Lazio since 2021.
It is also a DTC-approved research and innovation infrastructure laboratory with expertise and references in exploiting and optimizing research, communication, and disseminating project results.
In addition, the company has over 100 European and international partners worldwide, with whom it participates in projects for Horizon Europe and internationally.
The list of major academic partners includes Sapienza, Tor Vergata, Roma3, Imperial College London, the University of Malaga, the Technical University of Kosice, the University of Haifa, Aalborg University, the Polytechnic University of Barcelona, Helwan University in Cairo, and Al-Balqa University in Jordan.
The primary research and innovation organizations include the CNR, the INFN, the ENEA, and the Institute of Communication and Information Systems of Athens.
The public administration includes the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in Ankara and the Ministry of Culture in Tunisia.
Private partners include L Global (USA), ClioMuse Tours, Khora, LiveViewStudio, SQLI Services, Holusion, and Setur.
Vianet has a collaboration agreement with Prof. Maurizio Forte, PhD, the William and Sue Gross Distinguished Professor of Classical Studies Art, Art History, and Visual Studies at Duke University (Durham, North Carolina), to develop generative AI for reconstructing ancient sites and environments. Prof. Forte was recently awarded the San Francesco Prize in Techno-Humanities 2024 for his work in Digital Humanities.
 
Recent Projects:
- Pluggy, EU grant no. 726765, https://Pluggy.eu
- 3D Tuning In, EU grant no. 644051, https://3d-tune-in.eu/
- Artemisia, DTC Lazio, https://www.dtclazio.it/artemisia-infn

- ENGAGE, tba

Vianet upholds the elimination of discrimination in employment and occupation. We contribute to the enjoyment of rights, including those based on gender, race, religion, color, or disability.

entityDescription:
ECU - Energy and culture a cultural change for the intelligent and sustainable use of energy.
Founded in 2001, it is listed n.ro 52131AVK of the National Research Registry. He deals with promotion, consulting and technological assistance for business development programs and projects. Since 2013 it has been part of the Smart Power System High Technology District, born with the support of public funding PON 2013-2017 and participated in the project "MICCA- Microgrid Hybrids in Direct Current and Alternating Current", which ended positively in September 2017. The Project, in which the Universities of Campania, ENEA, CNR and a sufficient number of small and medium-sized enterprises participated, analyzes and provides solutions to the problem created by the introduction of an increasing number of distributed storage generation systems and rapidly variable loads that require electrical networks to meet the growing needs of flexibility, accessibility, reliability and quality of electrical service , economy and energy efficiency. The primary activities were the analysis and definition of requirements, functions, processes, design and testing of technologies with prototypes and demonstrators, technical-economic evaluations and interventions for energy saving and improvement of sustainability.
Other evidence of the ECU's activities in the field of scientific research and prototype development in collaboration with public research bodies, in particular for the use of their laboratories. An example of particular interest is the "Personal Safeguard Prototype" project. Monitoring and assistance system for people at significant risk, carried out with the participation of the research laboratory of the Federico II University of Neaples (Prof. A. Cutolo) on the basis of a patent registered at the Neaples Chamber of Commerce and funded by ASI - Italian Space Agency.
Other important examples: the "Prototype of Innovative HeartBeat Detection", realized with the CNR-IMM Laboratory of Neaples (Prof. I. Rendina), and the "Prototype of optically controlled absorption cell prototype" was created by the INFM laboratory (Prof.
The core business of the ECU is the promotion of an efficient use of energy resources, moving from a linear and expensive economy to a clean and circular economy. To this end, we associate energy issues with cultural issues: the aim of the ECU is to carry out projects that will accompany businesses with a sustainable transition. Through the proposal of innovative technologies and, accompanied by energy diagnoses and specific energy saving solutions, ECU offers solutions for different sectors: Public Administration, Health, Industry, Private. Consultancy, design and implementation are the phases of ECU solutions, independent of each other and at the same time integrated through the common thread of efficiency, effectiveness and cost-effectiveness. The use of innovative technologies concerns the objectives of efficiency, effectiveness and sustainability of the Circular Economy. Our projects aim to develop integrated systems with innovative components capable of managing multi-directional power flows, monitoring and adjusting voltage profiles, improving network stability even against power quality problems, developing Microgrid architectures for charging various types of full electric and plug-in vehicles; conversion and storage equipment, as well as evaluate energy exchange strategies also with renewable sources.

Azienda Mobilità e Trasporti S.p.A. (AMT) is the mobility company owned by the City of Genova, the capital and biggest city in the Liguria Region (northern western Italy).
AMT is in charge of providing public transport to the Metropolitan City of Genoa, both in urban and extra-urban territory.
By a multi-modal transport system, counting over 130 million transfers per year covering 27 million kilometers, AMT suits the Genoese transport requirements best.
The multi-modal system is granted by different means of transport: 900 buses and trolley buses, a subway, 2 funicular railways, 13 public elevators, a cog railway, a narrow-gauge railway, an urban ferry-boat and on-call services.
AMT is interested in favoring the ecological transition, monitoring the environment in which it provides its transport service and, in general, improving the service offered by paying particular attention to customers.

entityDescription:
S.A.C. (Società Appalti Costruzioni) is a construction company that belongs to the Cerasi family from Rome. S.A.C. has a share capital of � 8.400.000 and has been operating in the field of civil building, restoration, and major industrial and infrastructural works for the last 50 years. The Company deals with public contracts but also private works, executing interventions by its own capital, as well as real estate operations. Moreover, it has a leading position in different important company associations, consortia and societies (subsidiaries and associated) and companies, leaders in important urban renovation projects.
The family has cultivated over the years a great passion for art, creating an important collection of paintings and sculptures of the early 20thCentury Roman School (Balla, Sironi, De Chirico, Donghi, Mafai, Capogrossi, Casorati, Campigli, Severini and many other artists), culminating with the creation of the “Elena and Claudio Cerasi Foundation”. The family decided to make available to the community the entire collection of Palazzo Merulana, renovated for this purpose by SAC with the Project Financing procedure, in partnership with the City of Rome. Today the Palace has become an important cultural hub, reference point in the Esquilino district.

entityDescription: The Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. (FVB) represents seven (on 01 January 2021 one of formerly eight institutes left the FVB) research institutes of natural sciences, life sciences and environmental sciences in Berlin, which pursue common interests within the framework of a single legal entity while maintaining their scientific autonomy. As research institutions of supra-regional importance and national interest regarding science policy, the institutes are financed within the bounds of the joint research funding by the federal and state governments in accordance with article 91 b of the Basic Law. The institutes share an administrative infrastructure (“joint administration”) and are members of the Leibniz Association.
